chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-A'la ibn A'yan, the freedman of the family of Sam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Marry the virgins, for they are the best in terms of mouth (sweetness of speech), the most fertile in terms of bearing children, the best in terms of character, and the most open in terms of the womb. Do you not know that I boast about you to the nations on the Day of Resurrection, even about the fetus? It will remain swollen on the gate of Paradise, and God, the Mighty and Majestic, will say to it, 'Enter Paradise.' It will say, 'No, until my parents enter before me.' Then God, the Exalted, will say to one of the angels, 'Bring me its parents.' He will order them to be brought to Paradise, and He will say, 'This is by the grace of My mercy for you.'

key_terms.الْأَبْكَارَ: virgins (females who have not been married or had intercourse)
key_terms.الْأُمَمَ: the nations (of other prophets or peoples)
key_terms.مُحْبَنْطِئاً: swollen (referring to the fetus in the womb)

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues of marrying a virgin according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Prophet (peace be upon him) highlights the virtues of virgins, emphasizing their purity and fertility as signs of divine mercy. He illustrates the profound status of the faithful by describing how even a fetus will intercede for its parents, showcasing the cascading nature of Paradise's rewards. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on family continuity and the spiritual interconnectedness of generations within the divine covenant.
